articleTitle: Linear subvarieties of hypersurfaces
abstract: We give a sharp upper bound on the dimension of the Fano variety of k-planes in a smooth hypersurface in p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, when k ≥ (n−1)/4.

articleTitle: A note on steady gravity waves with vorticity
abstract: For an arbitrary nonpositive vorticity, we prove the existence of steady periodic two-dimensional gravity waves.

articleTitle: Geometric approach to error-correcting codes and reconstruction of signals
abstract: We develop an approach through geometric functional analysis to reconstruction of signals from few linear measurements and to error-correcting codes. An error-correcting code encodes an n-letter word x into an m-letter word y in such a way that x can be decoded correctly when any r letters of y are corrupted. We show that most linear orthogonal transformations Q: ℝn → ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> form efficient and robust error-correcting codes over reals. The decoder (which corrects the corrupted components of y) is the metric projection onto the range of Q in the ℓ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-norm. This yields robust error-correcting codes over reals (and over alphabets of polynomial size), with a Gilbert-Varshamov type bound, and with quadratic time encoders and polynomial time decoders. An equivalent problem arises in signal processing: how to reconstruct a signal that belongs to a small class from few linear measurements? We prove that for most sets of Gaussian measurements, all signals of small support can be exactly reconstructed by the L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-norm minimization. This is an improvement of recent results of Donoho and of Candes and Tao. An equivalent problem in combinatorial geometry is the existence of “neighborly” symmetric polytopes, that is, polytopes with fixed number of facets and maximal number of lower-dimensional facets. We prove that most sections of a cube form such polytopes. Our work thus belongs to a common ground of coding theory, signal processing, combinatorial geometry, and geometric functional analysis. Our argument, which is based on concentration of measure and improving Lipschitzness by random projections, may be of independent interest in geometric functional analysis.

articleTitle: Second-order difference equations and discrete orthogonal polynomials of two variables
abstract:
The second-order partial difference equation of two variables <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$	ext{D}u:=A_{1,1}{(x)}\Delta_1
abla_1u+A_{1,2}{(x)}\Delta_1
abla_2u+A_{2,1}{(x)}\Delta_2
abla_1u+A_{2,2}{(x)}\Delta_2
abla_2u+B_1{(x)}\Delta_1u+$</tex> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_2{(x)}\Delta_2u=\lambda u$</tex> is studied to determine when it has orthogonal polynomials as solutions. We derive conditions on D so that a weight function W exists for which W D u is selfadjoint and the difference equation has polynomial solutions which are orthogonal with respect to W. The solutions are essentially the classical discrete orthogonal polynomials of two variables.

articleTitle: Distribution functions for edge eigenvalues in orthogonal and symplectic ensembles: Painlevé representations
abstract: We derive Painlevé-type expressions for the distribution of the mth largest eigenvalue in the Gaussian orthogonal and symplectic ensembles in the edge scaling limit. This work generalizes to general m the m=1 results of Tracy and Widom (1996). The results of Johnstone (2001) and Soshnikov (2002) imply the immediate relevance of our formulas for the mth largest eigenvalue of the appropriate Wishart distribution.

articleTitle: On the extremality of Hofer's metric on the group of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms
abstract: Let M be a closed symplectic manifold, and let |·| be a norm on the space of all smooth functions on M, which are zero-mean normalized with respect to the canonical volume form. We show that if |·| ≤ C|·|<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> and |·| is invariant under the action of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms, then it is also invariant under all volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. We also prove that if |·| is, additionally, not equivalent to |·|<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>, then the induced pseudodistance function on the group Ham (M,ω) of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of M vanishes identically. These results provide partial answers to questions raised by Eliashberg and Polterovich in 1993. Both results rely on an extension of |·| to the space of essentially bounded measurable functions, which is invariant under all measure-preserving bijections.

articleTitle: Averages of ratios of characteristic polynomials for the compact classical groups
abstract: Averages of ratios of characteristic polynomials for the compact classical groups are evaluated in terms of determinants whose dimensions are independent of the matrix rank. These formulas are shown to be equivalent to expressions for the same averages obtained in a previous study, which was motivated by applications to analytic number theory. Our approach uses classical methods of random matrix theory, in particular determinants and orthogonal polynomials, and can be considered more elementary than the method of Howe pairs used in the previous study.

articleTitle: Transcendence of values at algebraic points for certain higher-order hypergeometric functions
abstract: We describe the exceptional set of a function studied by Picard. This is the set of algebraic points at which the function takes algebraic values. In particular, we deduce necessary and sufficient conditions for the finiteness of the exceptional set. Some of our results depend on recent conjectures of Pink.

articleTitle: On the exponent of the group of points on elliptic curves in extension fields
abstract: Let E be an elliptic curve defined over F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf>, a finite field of q elements. We show that the exponent of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf E{({\text{F}}_qn)}$</tex> , the group of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\textbf{F}}_\mathbf q\mathbf n$</tex> -rational points on E, is sufficiently large when q is fixed and n → ∞. This is an analogue of several results of Duke and Schoof on the exponent of the group E(F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>) of F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>-rational points, when a fixed elliptic curve E is defined over ℚ and the prime p → ∞.

articleTitle: Spectral asymptotics for periodic fourth-order operators
abstract: We consider the operator d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>/dt<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>+V on the real line with a real periodic potential V. The spectrum of this operator is absolutely continuous and consists of intervals separated by gaps. We define a Lyapunov function which is analytic on a two-sheeted Riemann surface. On each sheet, the Lyapunov function has the same properties as in the scalar case, but it has branch points, which we call resonances. We prove the existence of real as well as nonreal resonances for specific potentials. We determine the asymptotics of the periodic and antiperiodic spectra and of the resonances at high energy. We show that there exist two types of gaps: (1) stable gaps, where the endpoints are periodic and antiperiodic eigenvalues, (2) unstable (resonance) gaps, where the endpoints are resonances (i.e., real branch points of the Lyapunov function above the bottom of the spectrum). We also show that the periodic and antiperiodic spectra together determine the spectrum of our operator. Finally, we show that for small potentials V ≠ 0 the spectrum in the lowest band has multiplicity 4 and the bottom of the spectrum is a resonance, and not a periodic (or antiperiodic) eigenvalue.

articleTitle: Higher connectivity of graph coloring complexes
abstract: The main result of this paper is a proof of the following conjecture of Babson and Kozlov: letG be a graph of maximal valencyd; then the complex Hom(G,K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>) is at least (n-d-2) -connected. Here Hom(-,-) denotes the polyhedral complex introduced by Lovász to study the topological lower bounds for chromatic numbers of graphs. We will also prove, as a corollary to the main theorem, that the complex Hom(C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r+1</inf>,K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>) is (n−4)-connected, for n ≥ 3.

articleTitle: Double exponential sums related to Diffie-Hellman distributions
abstract: We establish the bound <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum\nolimits_{x\in X}{\vert\sum\nolimits_{y\in Y}\gamma{(y)}\exp\operatorname\pi{(2\pi ia\lambda^{xy}/p)}\vert}\ll{\vert X\vert}^{1/2}$</tex> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times{\vert Y\vert}^{1/2}p^{9/8+\varepsilon}/T^{1/4}$</tex> , where λ is of multiplicative order T modulo a large prime p, X and Y are arbitrary subsets of the residue ring modulo p−1 with |X| and |Y| elements correspondingly, γ(n) are any complex numbers with |γ(n)|≤ 1, and ε is any small positive constant. In particular cases, our estimate improves a series of the existing results.

articleTitle: The Mordell-Lang theorem for Drinfeld modules
abstract: We study the ring of quasi-endomorphisms for certain infinitely definable subgroups in separably closed fields. Based on the results we obtain, we are able to prove a Mordell-Lang theorem for Drinfeld modules of finite characteristic. Using specialization arguments, we prove also a Mordell-Lang theorem for Drinfeld modules of generic characteristic.

articleTitle: Nagata dimension, quasisymmetric embeddings, and Lipschitz extensions
abstract: We investigate a variant of Gromov's notion of asymptotic dimension that was introduced and named Nagata dimension by Assouad. This turns out to be a quasisymmetry invariant of metric spaces. The class of metric spaces with finite Nagata dimension includes doubling spaces, Gromov hyperbolic spaces of bounded local geometry, Euclidean buildings, and homogeneous Hadamard manifolds, among others, and is closed under taking finite products and finite unions. We prove a quasisymmetric embedding theorem and two comprehensive Lipschitz extension theorems involving a bound on the Nagata dimension.

articleTitle: On uniform bounds for rational points on nonrational curves
abstract: We show that the number of rational points of height ≤ H on a nonrational plane curve of degree d is O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>(H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/d−δ</sup>, for some δ > 0, depending only on d. The implicit constant depends only on d. This improves a result of Heath-Brown, who proved the bound O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ε</inf>(H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/d+ε</sup>). We also show that one can take δ = 1/450 in the case d=3.

articleTitle: Moduli spaces for semistable honest singular principal bundles on a nodal curve which are compatible with degeneration—a remark on Bhosle's paper “tensor fields and singular principal bundles”
abstract: Let G be a semisimple linear algebraic group and X a nodal curve. We show that if ρ : G → O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(ℂ)(Sp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(ℂ)) is a faithful representation and if δ⋙ 0, then any δ-semistable singular G-bundle is actually a principal G-bundle away from the node of X. Furthermore, we considerably simplify the notion of δ-(semi)stability.

articleTitle: Homological representations of the Iwahori-Hecke algebra associated with a Selberg-type integral
abstract: We construct an irreducible representation of the Iwahori-Hecke algebra on the twisted homology group, especially on the space of the regularizable cycles, associated with a Selberg-type integral. This representation is realized under some resonance condition on the exponents of the integral.

articleTitle: Stable determination of generic simple metrics from the hyperbolic Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
abstract: We prove Hölder-type stability estimates near generic simple Riemannian metrics for the inverse problem of recovering such metrics from the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map associated to the wave equation for the Laplace-Beltrami operator.

articleTitle: On Bethe vectors in the slN+1 Gaudin model
abstract: This paper deals with the Gaudin model associated with the tensor product of n irreducible finite-dimensional sl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N+1</inf>-modules marked by distinct complex numbers z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. The Bethe Ansatz is a method to construct common eigenvectors of the Gaudin Hamiltonians by means of chosen singular vectors in the factors and z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf>'s. These vectors are called Bethe vectors. The question if the Bethe vectors are nonzero vectors is open. By the moment, the only way to verify that was based on a relation to critical points of the master function of the Gaudin model, and nontriviality of a Bethe vector was proved only in the case when the corresponding critical point is nondegenerate. However degenerate critical points do appear in the Gaudin model. We believe that the Bethe vectors never vanish, and suggest an approach that does not depend on nondegeneracy of the corresponding critical point. The idea is for a Bethe vector to choose a suitable subspace in the weight space and to check that the projection of the Bethe vector to this subspace is nonzero. We apply this approach to verify nontriviality of Bethe vectors in new examples.

articleTitle: A proof of Huppert's ρ-σ conjectures for nonsolvable groups
abstract: We prove Huppert's ρ-σ conjecture for nonsolvable groups. This conjecture asserts that the cardinality of the set of primes that divide the degree of some irreducible character of a finite group is bounded in terms of the maximum number of different prime divisors of the irreducible characters of the group. We also settle the analogous problem for conjugacy class sizes.

articleTitle: On hyperbolicity of toric real threefolds
abstract: We prove that there is no smooth complex toric projective threefold X with a real part diffeomorphic to a hyperbolic manifold. In addition, we give an explicit example of a real projective toric threefold with a real part homeomorphic to a hyperbolic manifold.

articleTitle: Families of Painlevé VI equations having a common solution
abstract: We classify all functions satisfying nontrivial families of Painlevé VI equations. Each family is parameterized by an affine space. This affine space, except for the so-called constant families, is generated by points of “geometric origin,” associated either to deformations of elliptic surfaces with four singular fibers or to deformations of three-sheeted covers of ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> with branching locus consisting of four points.

articleTitle: Generalized cluster complexes and Coxeter combinatorics
abstract: We introduce and study a family of simplicial complexes associated to an arbitrary finite root system and a nonnegative integer parameter m. For m = 1, our construction specializes to the (simplicial) generalized associahedra or, equivalently, to the cluster complexes for the cluster algebras of finite type. Our computation of the face numbers and h-vectors of these complexes produces the enumerative invariants defined in other contexts by C. A. Athanasiadis, suggesting links to a host of well-studied problems in algebraic combinatorics of finite Coxeter groups, root systems, and hyperplane arrangements. Recurrences satisfied by the face numbers of our complexes lead to combinatorial algorithms for determining Coxeter-theoretic invariants. That is, starting with a Coxeter diagram of a finite Coxeter group, one can compute the Coxeter number, the exponents, and other classical invariants by a recursive procedure that only uses most basic graph-theoretic concepts applied to the input diagram.

articleTitle: The mean curvature flow approach to the symplectic isotopy problem
abstract: Let M be a Kähler-Einstein surface with positive scalar curvature. If the initial surface is sufficiently close to a holomorphic curve, we show that the mean curvature flow has a global solution and it converges to a holomorphic curve.

articleTitle: Construction of hypergeometric solutions to the q-Painlevé equations
abstract: Hypergeometric solutions to the q-Painlevé equations are constructed by direct linearization of discrete Riccati equations. The decoupling factors are explicitly determined so that the linear systems give rise to q-hypergeometric equations.

articleTitle: Integral affine structures on spheres: complete intersections
abstract: We give a construction of integral affine structures on spheres which conjecturally arise in the maximal degeneration limits of Calabi-Yau complete intersection families in toric varieties. This generalizes our model for affine structures on toric Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces.

articleTitle: The image of the heat kernel transform on Riemannian symmetric spacesof the noncompact type
abstract: The heat kernel transform on G/K, a Riemannian symmetric space of noncompact type, maps an L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-function on G/K to a holomorphic function on the complex crown. In this paper, we determine the image of this transform on L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A monodromy criterion for extending curves
abstract: A family of proper smooth curves of genus ≥ 2, parametrized by an open dense subset U of a normal variety S, extends to S if the natural map π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> U → π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> S is an isomorphism. The criterion of this paper is actually more precise.

articleTitle: Théorème limite central pour les endomorphismesholomorphes et les correspondances modulaires
abstract: Nous appliquons la méthode de Gordin pour obtenir un théorème limite central dans deux situations dynamiques différentes, celle des endomorphismes holomorphes de l'espace projectif et celle des correspondances modulaires. We apply the Gordin method to prove a central limit theorem for two families of dynamical systems: forward or backward iteration of holomorphic endomorphisms of projective spaces and iteration of modular correspondances.

articleTitle: A GUE central limit theorem and universality of directed first andlast passage site percolation
abstract: We prove a GUE central limit theorem for random variables with finite fourth moment. We apply this theorem to prove that the directed first and last passage percolation problems in thin rectangles exhibit universal fluctuations given by the Tracy-Widom law.

articleTitle: The integral basis problem of Eichler
abstract: For a quaternion algebra B over a totally real field F unramified at every finite place and ramified at most infinite places of F, we prove that the space of ℤ[1/E]-integral Hilbert modular forms of weight 2 and of level 1 is spanned over ℤ[1/E] by the theta series of the norm form of B. Here E=6d(F)∏<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ψ</inf> (the numerator of L(−1,ψ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>)), where d(F) is the discriminant of F and ψ runs over all unramified characters of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Gal}{(\overline F/F)}$</tex> .

articleTitle: On a vanishing problem of Demailly
abstract: A general vanishing theorem for the Dolbeault cohomology of a tensor product of symmetric and exterior powers of vector bundles is proved. It implies the solution to a problem of Demailly, a partial answer to which has been obtained by Manivel. The optimality of the result is shown by examples in a large range of parameters. Various ampleness criteria for vector bundles of independent interest are proved.

articleTitle: Blowup theory for the critical nonlinear Schrödinger equations revisited
abstract: We prove a refined version of compactness lemma adapted to the blowup analysis and we use it to give direct and simple proofs of some classical results of blowup theory for critical nonlinear Schrödinger equations.

articleTitle: Cherednik algebras and Yangians
abstract: We construct a functor from the category of modules over the trigonometric (resp., rational) Cherednik algebra of type gl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf> to the category of integrable modules of level l over a Yangian for the loop algebra sl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> (resp., over a subalgebra of this loop Yangian) and we establish that it is an equivalence of categories if l+2 < n. Finally, we treat the case of the rational Cherednik algebras of type A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l−1</inf>.

articleTitle: Multiples of subvarieties in algebraic groups over finite fields
abstract: Let X be a subvariety of a commutative algebraic group G over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\overset{\boldsymbol}{\textbf{F}}}_\mathbf q$</tex> such that X generates G. Then <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\boldsymbol\bigcup}_{\mathbf\varphi\boldsymbol\in\textbf{End}\mathbf G}\mathbf\varphi{\boldsymbol(\mathbf X{\boldsymbol({\overset{\boldsymbol}{\textbf{F}}}_\mathbf q\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol=\mathbf G{\boldsymbol({\overset{\boldsymbol�}{\textbf{F}}}_\mathbf q\boldsymbol)}$</tex> . If G is semiabelian, this can be strengthened to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\boldsymbol\bigcup}_{\mathbf n\boldsymbol\geq\mathbf1}\mathbf{nX}{\boldsymbol({\overset{\boldsymbol}{\textbf{F}}}_\mathbf q\boldsymbol)}\boldsymbol=\mathbf G{\boldsymbol({\overset{\boldsymbol}{\textbf{F}}}_\mathbf q\boldsymbol)}$</tex> , and there is a density-1 set of primes S such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf X{\boldsymbol({\overset{\boldsymbol�}{\textbf{F}}}_\mathbf q\boldsymbol)}$</tex> projects surjectively onto the S-primary part of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf G{\boldsymbol({\overset{\boldsymbol}{\textbf{F}}}_\mathbf q\boldsymbol)}$</tex> . These results build on work of Bogomolov and Tschinkel.

articleTitle: Precise asymptotics of the length spectrum for finite-geometry Riemann surfaces
abstract: We prove a prime orbit theorem with a precise error term for an arbitrary Riemann surface of finite geometry and infinite volume. The error term involves the low eigenvalues and the resonances of the Laplace-Beltrami operator.

articleTitle: Absolutely continuous spectrum of a class of random nonergodic Schrödinger operators
abstract: We consider a class of random Schrödinger operators with nondecaying potentials and prove that their absolutely continuous spectrum almost surely fills the positive half-line. We establish the existence of the wave operators using the trace-class scattering theory.

articleTitle: Stokes matrices for the quantum cohomologies of Grassmannians
abstract: We prove the conjectural relation between the Stokes matrix for the quantum cohomology of X and an exceptional collection generating D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sup> coh(X) when X is the Grassmannian Gr(r,n). The proof is based on the relation between the quantum cohomology of the Grassmannian and that of the projective space.

articleTitle: Diophantine m-tuples for primes
abstract: We show that if p is a prime and if A = {a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>,…,a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>} is a set of positive integers with the property that a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf>+p is a perfect square for all 1 ≤ i < j ≤ m, then m < 3 · 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">168</sup>. More generally, when p is replaced by a squarefree integer n, the inequality m ≤ f(ω(n)) holds with some function f, where ω(n) is the number of prime divisors of n. We also give upper bounds for m when p is replaced by an arbitrary integer which hold on a set of n of asymptotic density one.

articleTitle: Vanishing of eigenspaces and cyclotomic fields
abstract: We use a result of Thaine to give an alternative proof of the fact that, for a prime p>3 congruent to 3 modulo 4, the component e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(p+1)/2</inf> of the p-Sylow subgroup of the ideal class group of ℚ(ζ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>) is trivial.

articleTitle: Geometric Bessel models for GSp4 and multiplicity one
abstract: this paper, we study Bessel models of representations of GSp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> over a local nonarchimedian field in the framework of the geometric Langlands program. The Bessel module over the nonramified Hecke algebra of GSp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> admits a geometric counterpart, the Bessel category of perverse sheaves on some ind-algebraic stack. We use it to prove a geometric version of multiplicity one for Bessel models. It implies a geometric Casselman-Shalika-type formula for these models. We also propose a geometric framework unifying Whittaker, Waldspurger, and Bessel models.

articleTitle: Converging sequences of p-adic Galois representations and density theorems
abstract: We compare different notions of convergence for sequences of finite dimensional representations over a valued field. We then consider convergent sequences of Galois representations over ℂ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>, prove a control result for the component groups of the algebraic envelopes of the representations, and deduce a uniform Cebotarev-type density theorem for the representations in the sequence.

articleTitle: Uniform results for Serre's theorem for elliptic curves
abstract: A celebrated theorem of Serre from 1972 asserts that if E is an elliptic curve defined over ℚ and without complex multiplication, then its associated mod ℓ representation is surjective for all sufficiently large primes ℓ. In this paper we address the question of what “sufficiently large” means in Serre's theorem. More precisely, we obtain a uniform version of Serre's theorem for nonconstant elliptic curves defined over function fields, and a uniform version of Serre's theorem for one-parameter families of elliptic curves defined over ℚ.

articleTitle: Hochschild cohomology versus de Rham cohomology without formality theorems
abstract: We exploit the Fedosov-Weinstein-Xu (FWX) resolution proposed by A. Weinstein and P. Xu (1998) to establish an isomorphism between the ring of Hochschild cohomology of the quantum algebra of functions on a symplectic manifold M and the ring H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">•</sup>(M,ℂ(ħ)) of de Rham cohomology of M with the coefficient field ℂ((ħ)) without making use of any version of the formality theorem. We also show that the Gerstenhaber bracket induced on H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">•</sup>(M,ℂ(ħ)) via the isomorphism is vanishing. We discuss equivariant properties of the isomorphism and propose an analogue of this statement in an algebraic geometric setting.

articleTitle: Comparison of Poisson structures and Poisson-Lie dynamical r-matrices
abstract: We construct a Poisson isomorphism between the formal Poisson manifolds g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> and G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</inf>, where g is a finite-dimensional quasitriangular Lie bialgebra. Here g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> is equipped with its Lie-Poisson (or Kostant-Kirillov-Souriau) structure, and G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</inf> with its Poisson-Lie structure. We also quantize the Poisson-Lie dynamical r-matrices of Balog-Fehér-Palla.

articleTitle: Noncommutative double Bruhat cells and their factorizations
abstract: We study noncommutative double Bruhat cells in the group of invertible matrices over a noncommutative skew-field. For each noncommutative double Bruhat cell, we give explicit “positive” factorizations of matrices belonging to this cell. The factorizations of matrices are given in terms of quasiminors of these matrices.

articleTitle: Tableaux on periodic skew diagrams and irreducible representationsof the double affine Hecke algebra of type A
abstract: We introduce and study an affine analogue of skew Young diagrams and tableaux on them. It turns out that the double affine Hecke algebra of type A acts on the space spanned by standard tableaux on each diagram. It is shown that the modules obtained this way are irreducible, and they exhaust all irreducible modules of a certain class over the double affine Hecke algebra. In particular, the classification of irreducible modules of this class, announced by Cherednik, is recovered.

articleTitle: Estimates for singular multiplicative character sums
abstract: We give some estimates for multiplicative character sums on quasiprojective varieties over finite fields depending on the severity of the singularities of the variety at infinity. We also remove the hypothesis of nondivisibility by the characteristic of the base field in the known estimates for the nonsingular case.

articleTitle: Crystal of Lakshmibai-Seshadri paths associated to an integral weight of level zero for an affine Lie algebra
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda=\sum\nolimits_{i\in I_0}m_i\varpi_i$</tex> with m<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> ∈ ℤ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">≥0</inf> be an integral weight of level zero, where the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varpi_i$</tex> , i ∈ I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, are the level-zero fundamental weights for an affine Lie algebra g over ℚ, and let B(λ) be the crystal (with weight lattice P) of all Lakshmibai-Seshadri paths of shape λ. We define a crystal B(λ)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cl</inf> (with weight lattice P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cl</inf> ≔ P/(ℚ δ∩ P)) to be the set of paths cl(π) : [0, 1] → ℚ ⊗<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ℤ</inf> P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cl</inf> for π ∈ B(λ), where the path cl(π) is defined to be the composition of the path π :[0,1] → ℚ ⊗<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ℤ</inf> P with the canonical projection <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{cl}:\mathbb{Q}\otimes_\mathbb{Z}P\twoheadrightarrow \mathbb{Q}\otimes_\mathbb{Z}P_\text cl$</tex> . We prove that this crystal B(\λ)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cl</inf> is isomorphic to the tensor product <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\otimes_{i\in I_0}(\text{B}(\varpi_i)_\text cl)^{\otimes m_i}$</tex> of the crystals <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{B}(\varpi_i)_\text cl$</tex> , i ∈ I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, as a crystal with weight lattice P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cl</inf>. As a corollary, we obtain that for each integral weight λ ∈ P of level zero, the crystal B(λ)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cl</inf> is isomorphic, as a crystal with weight lattice P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cl</inf>, to the crystal base of a (certain) tensor product of the fundamental modules <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W{(\varpi_i)}$</tex> , i ∈ I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, of level zero over the quantized universal enveloping algebra U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf>′(g) of g over ℚ(q) with weight lattice P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cl</inf>.

articleTitle: New deformations of group algebras of Coxeter groups
abstract: We define new deformations of group algebras of Coxeter groups W and of subgroups of even elements in them by deforming the braid relations. We show that these deformations are algebraically flat if and only if they are formally flat, and that this happens if and only if the group W has no finite parabolic subgroups of rank 3. We explain the connection of our deformations with the Hecke algebras of orbifolds defined by the first author and with generalized double affine Hecke algebras defined by the authors and A. Oblomkov.

articleTitle: The Miura map on the line
abstract: We study relations between properties of the Miura map r ↦ q=B(r)=r′+r<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and Schrödinger operators L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf>=−d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/dx<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+q, where r and q are real-valued functions or distributions (possibly not decaying at infinity) from various classes. In particular, we study B as a map from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_\text{loc}^2{(\mathbb{R})}$</tex> to the local Sobolev space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_\text{loc}^{-1}{(\mathbb{R})}$</tex> , and the restriction of B to the Sobolev spaces Hrβ(ℝ) with rβ≥0. For example, we prove that the image of B on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_\text{loc}^{2}{(\mathbb{R})}$</tex> consists exactly of those <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q\in H_\text{loc}^{-1}{(\mathbb{R})}$</tex> such that the operator L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf> is positive. We also investigate mapping properties of the Miura map in these spaces. As an application, we prove an existence result for solutions of the Korteweg-de Vries equation in H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>(ℝ) for initial data in the range B(L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(ℝ)) of the Miura map.

articleTitle: On the quantum variance of matrix elements for the cat map on the 4-dimensional torus
abstract: For many classically chaotic systems, it is believed that in the semiclassical limit, the matrix elements of smooth observables approach the phase space average of the observable. In the approach to the limit, the matrix elements can fluctuate around this average. Here we study the variance of these fluctuations, for the quantum cat map on T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>. We show that for certain maps and observables, the variance has a different rate of decay than is expected for generic chaotic systems.

articleTitle: Large scale geometry of 4-dimensional closed nonpositivelycurved real analytic manifolds
abstract: We study the asymptotic cones of the universal covering spaces of closed 4-dimensional nonpositively curved real analytic manifolds. We show that the existence of nonstandard components in the Tits boundary, discovered by Christoph Hummel and Victor Schroeder (1998), depends only on the quasi-isometry type of the fundamental group.

articleTitle: Equidistribution of the horocycles of a geometrically finite surface
abstract: In this work, we prove equidistribution properties of the horocycles of a geometrically finite surface with variable negative curvature. In the hyperbolic case, we deduce an equidistribution result of the orbits of the horocyclic flow of a surface with infinite volume.

articleTitle: Complex dynamics and invariant forms mod p
abstract: Complex dynamical systems on the Riemann sphere do not possess “invariant forms.” However there exist nontrivial examples of dynamical systems, defined over number fields, satisfying the property that their reduction modulo ℘ possesses “invariant forms” for all but finitely many places ℘. The paper completely characterizes the dynamical systems possessing the latter property.

articleTitle: Bounded eigenfunctions in the real hyperbolic space
abstract: We characterize the distributions on the boundary of the hyperbolic space ℍ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> whose Poisson-Helgason transforms are bounded λ-eigenfunctions of the Laplace operator. Our main result states that these distributions are exactly the derivatives of Hölder functions on S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−1</sup>, whose smoothness order can be precisely expressed in terms of the eigenvalue λ; this extends the results obtained in the case n=2 by the second author.

articleTitle: Finitely ramified iterated extensions
abstract: Let K be a number field, t a parameter, F = K(t), and φ(x)∈ K [x] a polynomial of degree d ≥ 2. The polynomial Φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(x,t) = φ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">^n</sup> (x) − t ∈ F[x], where φ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">^ n</sup> = φ ^ φ ^ … ^ φ is the n-fold iterate of φ, is irreducible over F; we give a formula for its discriminant. Let F be the field obtained by adjoining to F all roots (in a fixed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\overline F$</tex> ) of Φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(x,t) for all n ≥ 1; its Galois group Gal(F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">φ</inf>/F) is the iterated monodromy group of φ. The iterated extension F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">φ</inf> is finitely ramified over F if and only if φ is postcritically finite. We show that, moreover, for post-critically finite φ, every specialization of F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">φ</inf>/F at t = t<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ∈ K is finitely ramified over K, pointing to the possibility of studying Galois groups of number fields with restricted ramification via tree representations associated to iterated monodromy groups of postcritically finite polynomials. We discuss the wildness of ramification in some of these representations, describe prime decomposition in terms of certain finite graphs, and also give some examples of monogène number fields that arise from the construction.

articleTitle: A singular Poincaré lemma
abstract: We prove a Poincaré lemma for a set of r smooth functions on a 2n-dimensional smooth manifold satisfying a commutation relation determined by r singular vector fields associated to a Cartan subalgebra of sp(2r,ℝ). This result has a natural interpretation in terms of the cohomology associated to the infinitesimal deformation of a completely integrable system.

articleTitle: Scattering amplitude for the Schrödinger equation with strong magnetic field and strong electric potential
abstract: We study the scattering amplitude for the Schrödinger equation with constant magnetic field. If the electric potential and the magnetic field have the same strength b, the behavior when b → + ∞ is semi-classical. Under a non-trapping condition, we approximate the scattering amplitude by a pseudo-differential operator.

articleTitle: Nonlinear wave interactions for the Benjamin-Ono equation
abstract: We study the interaction of suitable small and high frequency waves evolving by the flow of the Benjamin-Ono equation. As a consequence, we prove that the flow map of the Benjamin-Ono equation cannot be uniformly continuous on bounded sets of H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>(ℝ) for s>0.

articleTitle: Local estimates for some fully nonlinear elliptic equations
abstract: We present a method to derive local estimates for some classes of fully nonlinear elliptic equations. The advantage of our method is that we derive Hessian estimates directly from C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> estimates. Also, the method is flexible and can be applied to a large class of equations.

articleTitle: The large sieve inequality with exponential functions and the distribution of Mersenne numbers modulo primes
abstract: Let S be a set of T = # S positive integers in the interval [1,N] and let ϑ ≥ 2 be a fixed integer. We obtain a version of the large sieve inequality for the set ϑ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, n ∈ S. For example, if S is not too sparse, then the residues ϑ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>(mod p) are uniformly distributed for almost all primes in the interval [Q/2, Q] for a very wide range of values of Q. In the special case, when S is the set of primes of the interval [1,N], we use a different approach, which in particular implies that Mersenne numbers are uniformly distributed modulo p for almost all p. This complements a series of recent bounds, which are considerably weaker but instead apply to “individual” values of p rather than “on average.”

articleTitle: Formal deformations of morphisms of associative algebras
abstract: The L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>-algebra controlling simultaneous deformations of a morphism of associative algebras and its domain and codomain is described. Isomorphism of the cohomology of this L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>-algebra with the classical construction is shown.

articleTitle: On a class of double cosets in reductive algebraic groups
abstract: We study a class of double coset spaces R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf> \ G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> × G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> / R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>, where G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are connected reductive algebraic groups, and R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf> and R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf> are certain spherical subgroups of G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> × G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> obtained by “identifying” Levi factors of parabolic subgroups in G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Such double cosets naturally appear in the symplectic leaf decompositions of Poisson homogeneous spaces of complex reductive groups with the Belavin-Drinfel'd Poisson structures. They also appear in orbit decompositions of the De Concini-Procesi compactifications of semisimple groups of adjoint type. We find explicit parametrizations of the double coset spaces and describe the double cosets as homogeneous spaces of R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf> × R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</inf>. We further show that all such double cosets give rise to set-theoretical solutions to the quantum Yang-Baxter equation on unipotent algebraic groups.

articleTitle: A desingularization of real differentiable actions of finite groups
abstract: We provide abelianizations of differentiable actions of finite groups on smooth real manifolds. De Concini-Procesi wonderful models for (local) subspace arrangements and a careful analysis of linear actions on real vector spaces are at the core of our construction. In fact, we show that our abelianizations have stabilizers isomorphic to elementary abelian 2-groups, a setting for which we suggest the term digitalization. As our main examples, the resulting digitalizations of the permutation actions of the symmetric group on real linear and projective spaces are discussed.

articleTitle: A mirror conjecture for projective bundles
abstract: We propose, motivate, and give evidence for a relation between the D-modules of the quantum cohomology of a smooth complex projective manifold X and a projective bundle ℙ(⊕ L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>) over X.

articleTitle: On generalized sum rules for Jacobi matrices
abstract: This work is in a stream initiated by a paper of Killip and Simon (2003). Using methods of functional analysis and the classical Szegö theorem we prove sum rule identities in a very general form. Then, we apply the result to obtain new asymptotics for orthonormal polynomials.

articleTitle: Finite free entropy and free group factors
abstract: We show the existence of noncommutative random variables with finite free entropy but which do not generate a free group factor. In particular, this gives an example of variables X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> such that δ(X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>) = n while W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>(X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>) ≇ L(F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>).

articleTitle: Low-lying zeroes of symmetric power L-functions
abstract: We study the distribution of low lying zeroes assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis of symmetric power L-functions associated to cusp forms of weight k for SL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (ℤ) which are Hecke eigenforms. Following the theory of Katz and Sarnak and the approach of Iwaniec, Luo, and Sarnak (2000), we determine the symmetry type of the corresponding family of L-functions, thereby providing further evidence to the truth of density conjecture.

articleTitle: Dispersion and Strichartz inequalities for the one-dimensionalSchrödinger equation with variable coefficients
abstract: We study the dispersive properties of the solution to the Schrödinger equation in dimension 1 without an explicit formula of the solution, and we prove local Strichartz estimates for metrics g ∈ W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2,∞</sup>. In the constant coefficient Schrödinger equation case, the method used here provides the classical dispersion in all dimensions.

articleTitle: Curves in abelian varieties over finite fields
abstract: Over an algebraic closure of a finite field, we show that multiples of a curve generating an abelian variety cover the whole abelian variety. As a corollary, there exist varieties over such fields which are not covered by a family of rational curves but are nevertheless rationally connected. Over number fields, we prove that algebraic points on many Kummer type varieties can be approximated by points lying on rational curves.

articleTitle: Laplace transformations and spectral theory of two-dimensionalsemidiscrete and discrete hyperbolic Schrödinger operators
abstract: We introduce Laplace transformations of 2D semidiscrete hyperbolic Schrödinger operators and show their relation to a semidiscrete 2D Toda lattice. We develop the algebrogeometric spectral theory of 2D semidiscrete hyperbolic Schrödinger operators and solve the direct spectral problem for 2D discrete ones (the inverse problem for discrete operators was already solved by Krichever). Using the spectral theory, we investigate spectral properties of the Laplace transformations of these operators. This makes it possible to find solutions of the semidiscrete and discrete 2D Toda lattices in terms of Theta-functions.

articleTitle: Partially defined semigroups relative to multiplicative free convolution
abstract: Nica and Speicher have shown that every probability measure on the line belongs to a partial semigroup {μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf> : t ≥ 1} relative to additive free convolution (i.e., μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t+s</inf>=μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>⊞μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf> for t, s≥1). We prove analogous results for multiplicative free convolution on the positive half-line and on the circle. The existence of semigroups is derived from certain global inversion results for analytic functions defined on the disk or on the slit complex plane. A close analysis of the global inverses yields regularity results for the measures in these semigroups. We also use this analysis to improve the known results for the additive situation.

articleTitle: On discrete models of the Euler equation
abstract: We consider two discrete models for the Euler equation describing incompressible fluid dynamics. These models are infinite coupled systems of ODEs for the functions u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">j</inf> which can be thought of as wavelet coefficients of the fluid velocity. The first model has been proposed and studied by Katz and Pavlović. The second has been recently discussed by Waleffe and goes back to Obukhov's studies of the energy cascade in developed turbulence. These are the only basic models of this type satisfying some natural scaling and conservation conditions. We prove that the Katz-Pavlović model leads to finite-time blowup for any initial datum, while the Obukhov model has a global solution for any sufficiently smooth initial datum.

articleTitle: A Hopf algebra quantizing a necklace Lie algebra canonically associated to a quiver
abstract: Ginzburg, Bocklandt, and Le Bruyn defined an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra canonically associated to any quiver. Following suggestions of V. Turaev, P. Etingof, and Ginzburg, we define a cobracket and prove that it defines a Lie bialgebra structure. We then present a Hopf algebra quantizing this Lie bialgebra and prove that it is a Hopf algebra satisfying the Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt (PBW) property. We also define representations to differential operators quantizing the trace representations of the Lie algebra defined by Ginzburg.

articleTitle: Rational and trigonometric degeneration of the double affine Hecke algebra of type A
abstract: We study a connection between the representation theory of the rational Cherednik algebra of type GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> and the representation theory of the degenerate double affine Hecke algebra (the degenerate DAHA). We focus on an algebra embedding from the rational Cherednik algebra to the degenerate DAHA and investigate the induction functor through this embedding. We prove that this functor embeds the category O for the rational Cherednik algebra fully faithfully into the category O for the degenerate DAHA. We also study the full subcategory O<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ss</sup> of O consisting of those modules which are semisimple with respect to the commutative subalgebra generated by Cherednik-Dunkl operators. A classification of all irreducible modules in O<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ss</sup> for the rational Cherednik algebra is obtained from the corresponding result for the degenerate DAHA.

articleTitle: Lifting from $\widetilde{SL}(2)$ to GSpin(1,4)
abstract: We construct liftings of automorphic forms from the metaplectic group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde{SL}_{2}$</tex> to GSpin(1,4) using the Maaß converse theorem. In order to prove the non-vanishing of the lift, we derive Waldspurger's formula for Fourier coefficients of half-integer weight Maaß forms. We analyze the automorphic representation of the adelic spin group obtained from the lift and show that it is CAP to the Saito-Kurokawa lift from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde{SL}_{2}$</tex> to GSp<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>(A).

articleTitle: On growth rate near the blowup surface for semilinear wave equations
abstract: We find the optimal growth estimate near the blowup surface for the semilinear wave equation with a power nonlinearity. The techniques are based on local energy estimates of our earlier work, which extend to the present situation. The exponent p is superlinear and less than or equal to 1+4/(N−1) if N ≥ 2.

articleTitle: Local covering optimality of lattices: Leech lattice versus root lattice E8
abstract: We show that the Leech lattice gives a sphere covering which is locally least dense among lattice coverings. We show that a similar result is false for the root lattice E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>. For this we construct a less dense covering lattice whose Delone subdivision has a common refinement with the Delone subdivision of E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>. The new lattice yields a sphere covering which is more than 12% less dense than the formerly best known given by the lattice <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_8^\ast$</tex> . Currently, the Leech lattice is the first and only known example of a locally optimal lattice covering having a nonsimplicial Delone subdivision. We hereby in particular answer a question of Dickson posed in 1968. By showing that the Leech lattice is rigid, our answer is even the strongest possible in a sense.

articleTitle: Non-abelian descent and the arithmetic of Enriques surfaces
abstract: We give sufficient conditions for the composition of two torsors to be a torsor under the group which is an extension of the corresponding structure groups. This construction is applied to produce natural non-abelian torsors on the Enriques surfaces. We exhibit an Enriques surface over ℚ with a dense set of ℚ-points, which is a counterexample to weak approximation accounted for by the descent obstruction defined by such a non-abelian torsor, but not by the Brauer-Manin obstruction.

articleTitle: Determination of a GL3 cuspform by twists of central L-values
abstract: Let π be a self-contragredient cuspidal automorphic representation of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(Aℚ). We show that if the symmetric square L-function of π has a pole at s=1, then π is determined by central values of quadratic twists of its L-function. That is, if π′ is another cuspidal automorphic representation of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(Aℚ) for which L(1/2, π⊗χ)=L(1/2, π′ ⊗χ) for sufficiently many quadratic characters χ, then π≃π′.

articleTitle: Invariants additifs de dg-catégories
abstract: A l'aide des outils de l'algèbre homotopique de Quillen, on construit “l'invariant additif universel,” c'est-à-dire un foncteur défini sur la catégorie des petites dg-catégories et à valeurs dans une catégorie additive qui rend inversibles les dg-foncteurs de Morita, transforme les décompositions semi-orthogonales au sens de Bondal et Orlov (1995) en sommes directes et qui est universel pour ces propriétées. Nous comparons notre construction à celle de Bondal, Larsen, et Lunts (2004).With the help of the tools of Quillen's homotopical algebra, we construct “the universal additive invariant,” namely, a functor from the category of small dg categories to an additive category, that inverts the Morita dg functors, transforms the semi-orthogonal decompositions in the sense of Bondal and Orlov (1995) into direct sums and which is universal for these properties. We compare our construction with that of Bondal, Larsen, and Lunts (2004).

articleTitle: Connected components of spaces of surface group representations II
abstract: In our previous paper (2003), we discussed the connected components of the space of surface group representations for any compact connected semisimple Lie group and any closed compact (orientable or nonorientable) surface. In this sequel, we generalize our results in two directions: we consider general compact connected Lie groups, and we consider all compact surfaces, including the ones with boundaries. We also interpret our results in terms of moduli spaces of flat connections over compact surfaces.

articleTitle: Stability of the absolutely continuous spectrum for multidimensional Schrödinger operators
abstract: We consider the Schrödinger operators −▵+V in L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) with slowly decaying potentials V. We prove that the absolutely continuous spectrum of these operators is essentially supported by ℝ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</inf> provided V satisfies |V(x)|+|x||∇′ V(x)|≤C〈 x〉<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/2−ε</sup>, ε>0, ∇′ being the angular component of the gradient.

articleTitle: Global discrepancy and small points on elliptic curves
abstract: Let E be an elliptic curve defined over a number field k. In this paper, we define the “global discrepancy” of a finite set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z\subset E{(\overline k)}$</tex> which in a precise sense measures how far the set is from being adelically equidistributed. We prove an upper bound for the global discrepancy of Z in terms of the average canonical height of points in Z. We deduce from this inequality a number of consequences. For example, we give a new and simple proof of the Szpiro-Ullmo-Zhang equidistribution theorem for elliptic curves. We also prove a non-Archimedean version of the Szpiro-Ullmo-Zhang theorem which takes place on the Berkovich analytic space associated to E. We then prove some quantitative “non-equidistribution” theorems for totally real or totally p-adic small points. The results for totally real points imply similar bounds for points defined over the maximal cyclotomic extension of a totally real field.

articleTitle: A characterization for a class of weight matrices with orthogonal matrix polynomials satisfying second-order differential equations
abstract: We characterize the weight matrices of the forms $e^{-t^2}e^{At}e^{A^\ast t}$ , $e^{-t^2}e^{At^2}e^{A^\ast t^2}$ , $t^\alpha e^{-t}e^{At}e^{A^\ast t}$ , $t^\alpha e^{-t}t^At^{A^\ast}$ , and ${(1-t)}^\alpha{(1+t)}^\mathrm{r�}{(1\pm t)}^A{(1\pm t)}^{A^\ast}$ that give rise to orthogonal matrix polynomials satisfying a symmetric linear second-order differential equation with differential coefficients independent of n. Matrix polynomials with this extra property are very likely going to play in the case of matrix orthogonality a role as central as the one played by the classical families of Hermite, Laguerre, and Jacobi in the scalar one. The results hinge on finding all representations of certain commutation relations satisfied by A.>

articleTitle: BGG correspondence for projective complete intersections
abstract: We extend the BGG correspondence for coherent sheaves on projective spaces (Bernstein-Gelfand-Gelfand) or complete intersections of quadrics (Kapranov) to general projective complete intersections.

articleTitle: Relatively hyperbolic groups with rapid decay property
abstract: We prove that a finitely generated group G that is (strongly) relatively hyperbolic with respect to a collection of finitely generated subgroups {H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>} has the rapid decay property if and only if each H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>, i=1,2,…,m, has the rapid decay property.

articleTitle: Values of zeta functions at s=1/2
abstract: We study the behaviour near s=1/2 of zeta functions of varieties over finite fields F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf> with q a square. The main result is an Euler-characteristic formula for the square of the special value at s=1/2. The Euler-characteristic is constructed from the Weil-étale cohomology of a certain supersingular elliptic curve.

articleTitle: Self-shrinkers of the mean curvature flow in arbitrary codimension
abstract: We study self-similar solutions M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup> ⊂ ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> of the mean curvature flow in arbitrary codimension. Self-similar curves Γ⊂ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> have been completely classified by Abresch and Langer (1986) and this result can be applied to curves Γ⊂ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> equally well. A submanifold M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>⊂ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> is called spherical, if it is contained in a sphere. Obviously, spherical self-shrinkers of the mean curvature flow coincide with minimal submanifolds of the sphere. For hypersurfaces M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>⊂ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m+1</sup>, m ≥ 2, Huisken (1990) showed that compact self-shrinkers with positive scalar mean curvature are spheres. We will prove the following extension: a compact self-similar solution M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>⊂ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>, m ≥ 2, is spherical, if and only if the mean curvature vector H is nonvanishing and the principal normal ν is parallel in the normal bundle. We also give a classification of complete noncompact self-shrinkers of that type.

articleTitle: Links, two-handles, and four-manifolds
abstract: We show that only finitely many links in a closed 3-manifold can have homeomorphic complements, up to twists along discs and annuli. Using the same techniques, we prove that by adding 2-handles on the same link we get only finitely many smooth cobordisms between two given closed 3-manifolds. As a consequence, there are only finitely many closed smooth 4-manifolds constructed from some Kirby diagram with bounded number of crossings, discs, and strands, or from some Turaev special shadow with bounded number of vertices. (These are the 4-dimensional analogues of Heegaard diagrams and special spines for 3-manifolds.) We therefore get two filtrations on the set of all closed smooth orientable 4-manifolds with finite sets. The two filtrations are equivalent after linear rescalings, and their cardinality grows at least as n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c · n</sup>.

articleTitle: Asymptotic dimension of relatively hyperbolic groups
abstract: Suppose that a finitely generated group G is hyperbolic relative to a collection of subgroups {H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>}. We prove that if each of the subgroups H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> has finite asymptotic dimension, then asymptotic dimension of G is also finite.

articleTitle: OPE-algebras and their modules
abstract: Vertex algebras formalize the subalgebra of holomorphic fields of a conformal field theory. OPE-algebras were proposed by Kapustin and Orlov as a generalization of vertex algebras that formalizes the algebra of all fields of a conformal field theory. We prove some basic results about them. The state-field correspondence is an OPE-algebra isomorphism and Dong's lemma and the existence theorem hold for multiply local OPE-algebras. Locality implies skew-symmetry. If skew-symmetry holds, then duality implies locality for modules and they are equivalent for algebras. We define modules over OPE-algebras.

articleTitle: A bilinear Fourier extension theorem and applications to the distance set problem
abstract: We obtain a weighted version of Tao's bilinear Fourier extension estimate for elliptic surfaces. This implies improved partial results in the direction of Falconer's distance set conjecture in dimensions d ≥ 3.

articleTitle: Homological realization of restricted Kostka polynomials
abstract: We give two realizations of restricted Kostka polynomials for sl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Firstly we identify restricted Kostka polynomials with characters of the zero homology of the current algebra with coefficients in the certain modules. As a corollary we reobtain the alternating sum formula. Secondly we show that restricted Kostka polynomials are q-multiplicities of the decomposition of the certain integrable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widehat{{\text{sl}}_2}$</tex> -modules to the irreducible components. This allows to write a kind of fermionic formula for the Virasoro unitary characters.

articleTitle: Hermitian-holomorphic Deligne cohomology, Deligne pairing for singular metrics, and hyperbolic metrics
abstract: We introduce a model for Hermitian-holormorphic Deligne cohomology on a projective algebraic manifold which allows to incorporate singular Hermitian structures along a normal crossing divisor. In the case of a projective curve, the cup product in cohomology is shown to correspond to a generalization of the Deligne pairing to line bundles with “good” Hermitian metrics in the sense of Mumford and others. A particular case is that of the tangent bundle of the curve twisted by the negative of the singularity divisor of a hyperbolic metric: its cup square (corrected by the total area) is shown to be a functional whose extrema are the metrics of constant negative curvature.

articleTitle: Localization lengths for Schrödinger operators on ℤ2 with decaying random potentials
abstract: We study a class of Schrödinger operators on ℤ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a random potential decaying as |x|<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−σ</sup>, 0<σ≤1/2, in the limit of small disorder strength λ. For the critical exponent σ=1/2, we prove that the localization length of eigenfunctions is bounded below by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{\lambda^{-1/4+\eta}}$</tex> , while for 0<σ<1/2, the lower bound is λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−(2−η)/(1−2σ)</sup>, for any η>0. These estimates “interpolate” between the lower bound λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2+η</sup> due to recent work of Schlag-Shubin-Wolff for σ=0, and pure a.c. spectrum for σ>1/2 demonstrated in recent work of Bourgain.

articleTitle: Spherical transform and Jacobi polynomials on root systems of type BC
abstract: Let R be a root system of type BC in a = ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sup> with general positive multiplicities. We introduce a certain canonical weight function on a which in the case of symmetric domains corresponds to the integral kernel of the Berezin transform. We compute its spherical transform and prove a Bernstein-Sato-type formula. This generalizes earlier work of Unterberger and Upmeier, van Dijk-Pevzner, Neretin, and the author. Associated to the weight function there are Heckman-Opdam orthogonal polynomials of Jacobi type on the compact torus; after a change of variables they form an orthogonal system on the noncompact space a. We prove that their spherical transforms are the multivariable Wilson polynomials multiplied by the spherical transform of the canonical weight function. For the rank one case, this was proved earlier by Koornwinder.

articleTitle: Equivariant embeddings of trees into hyperbolic spaces
abstract: We exhibit for any tree a family of equivariant embeddings into infinite-dimensional real hyperbolic spaces and study their geometric properties. For the automorphism group of a regular tree of finite valency, we classify all isometric actions on such hyperbolic spaces.

articleTitle: The N-eigenvalue problem and two applications
abstract: We consider the classification problem for compact Lie groups G ⊂ U(n) which are generated by a single conjugacy class with a fixed number N of distinct eigenvalues. We give an explicit classification when N=3, and apply this to extract information about Galois representations and braid group representations.

articleTitle: Uniqueness for steady periodic water waves with vorticity
abstract: For arbitrary vorticity, we prove uniqueness for steady periodic waves propagating at the surface of water with a flat bed: the surface profile and the vorticity distribution determine the motion within the entire fluid domain. The result holds with or without surface tension and gravity.

articleTitle: Reduction of CM elliptic curves and modular function congruences
abstract: Here we investigate congruences for the coefficients of modular functions on SL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(ℤ). We obtain a simple criterion, in terms of the locus of supersingular j-invariants, which guarantees certain congruences. We implement this criterion in the case of modular functions obtained from Hilbert class polynomials.

articleTitle: Approximation by power series with ± 1 coefficients
abstract: We construct certain type of near-optimal approximations of a class of analytic functions in the unit disc by power series with two distinct coefficients. More precisely, we show that if the coefficients of the power series f(z) = ∑ a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> z<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> are all real and lie in [-μ,μ], where μ < 1, then there exists a power series Q(z) = ∑ q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> with coefficients in {−1, +1} such that |f(z)-Q(z)| → 0 at the rate e<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−C/|1−z|</sup> as z → 1 nontangentially inside the unit disc. A result by Borwein, Erdélyi, and Kós shows that this type of decay rate is best possible. The special case f ≡ 0 yields a near-optimal solution to the “fair duel” problem of Konyagin.

articleTitle: Planar open books and Floer homology
abstract: Giroux has described a correspondence between open book decompositions on a 3-manifold and contact structures. In this paper we use Heegaard Floer homology to give restrictions on contact structures which correspond to open book decompositions with planar pages, generalizing a recent result of Etnyre.

articleTitle: High-frequency smooth solutions and well-posedness of the Camassa-Holm equation
abstract: We construct high-frequency smooth periodic solutions to the Camassa-Holm equation and use them to prove that the related solution map is not uniformly continuous on bounded sets in any Sobolev space of index greater than or equal to two.

articleTitle: Monodromy of the Hitchin map over hyperelliptic curves
